touches.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank.
Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
A device holds machines and uses tools (1.3.1).
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).
rehearsal: the cheapest model reads a ticket cold and tries to build it on paper, saying where it got stopped or what is missing.
PURPOSE: training data, so graph trees learn to judge "buildable as written" without an LLM call.

WHY: a simulation costs tokens; it earns them only by teaching a tree. It was never meant to catch every shortcoming of every ticket, and where it teaches nothing it costs more than the builder simply building and recording where it got stuck. So until a learner reads the records, a rehearsal is not a BUILDME requirement; the records stand as the learner's first corpus.

The read is handed the plan steps, the frame (intention, why, falsifier), and what exists and what does not, measured before the read. "Cold" means no conversation, history, chart or process, not blind to the disk.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
